theoryPrediction.theoremScope: Any two nonzero packet-density functions in the same nonzero constant metric gradient.

source.citation: Touboul et al. (2022), MICROSCOPE mission final results
Lee et al. (2020), New Test of the Gravitational 1/r^2 Law at Separations down to 52 micrometers
source.publishedConclusion: Newtonian gravity gives an excellent fit; alpha=1 Yukawa ranges must be below 38.6 micrometers at 95% confidence.

prediction.underTotalGradientClosure: The microscopic conductivity and its derivative are indistinguishable from unity; incremental laboratory gravity is Newtonian inverse-square.
prediction.publishedSensitivityScale: percent-level determination of Newtonian gravity at about 50 micrometers
prediction.compatibilityCriterion: both conductivity-deficit and derivative bounds below 1e-2

verdict.openDerivation: The canonical packet model proves universality for arbitrary density profiles, but it does not yet derive from Standard-Model microphysics that chemically different Ti and Pt bodies map only to that universal density coupling. A direct nonlinear reconstruction of the Eot-Wash apparatus geometry is also open.
